Patch Set 15:

(16 comments)

Experimental feature testing in progress, please pay attention to the comments

Some concerns, see inline comments. The two biggest are the cld_lockh handling in mgc_process_log() and the fact that OBD_CONNECT_FTM aliases OBD_CONNECT_MDS_MDS, so setting it on the client MGC import silently reaches generic MDS-MDS code in ldlm_lockd.c, ptlrpc/import.c and (via the new pinger hunk) every OSP/LWP import. The do_config_log_add() error-path fix is a separate bug from b2e9c58000 and would be better squashed there.

Patch Set 20:

(10 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Some concerns, see inline comments. The main ones are in mgc_request.c: the new client_import_add_nids_to_conn() block in mgc_apply_recover_logs() re-takes the MGC cl_sem that do_requeue() already holds for read, and the new local lock cancel in do_requeue() re-arms cld_lostlock through the synchronous cancel callback so the requeue never settles. It would also be easier to review if the MGC lock-handling fixes (do_config_log_add() label, do_requeue(), mgc_requeue_add()) and the mgs_nids.c assertion change were split out from the FTM feature itself.

Patch Set 21:

(13 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Some concerns, see inline comments. The new err_exp label in do_config_log_add() puts cld_mgcexp twice, and the new with_imp_locked(mgc, ...) in mgc_apply_recover_logs() re-takes cl_sem that do_requeue() already holds for read - both look like they need a fix before this lands.

Several hunks in mgc_request.c and mgs_nids.c are not described in the commit message; it would help review a lot if they were either explained or split out. The sanity test_27Ce failures raised on patch set 18 still look unaddressed - the random connection priority discussed inline makes the client MGC prefer a freshly discovered follower over the configured MGS on the next reconnect, which is a plausible route to reading stale pool config.

Uploaded patch set 22.

Patch Set 24:

(14 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Some concerns, see inline comments. The ones worth a second look are the no-op handle reset that replaced the LASSERT in mgc_process_log(), the SSK key-description mismatch that the server MGC rename introduces, the head/tail coin flip used to "shuffle" MGS NIDs, and the -ENOENT to -EAGAIN change that removes the only way an IR requeue loop can terminate. The patch also folds in several independent changes (an export refcount leak fix in do_config_log_add(), the MGC lock-handle rework, and the MGS error-code change) that would be easier to review, land and bisect as separate patches.

Patch Set 30:

(7 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Some concerns, see inline comments. Beyond the FTM feature itself, this change also carries several independent fixes to code the earlier patches in this series (and one landed patch) touched: the cld_mgcexp reference leak in do_config_log_add(), the stale-lock handling in mgc_blocking_ast() that replaces an LASSERT, the version-sorted insertion in mgs_follower_nidtbl_update(), and the 'rc = 0' additions before the continue statements in mgc_apply_recover_logs(). Each of those is a self-contained fix that could land on its own (or be folded into the patch that introduced the problem), and separating them would make both the feature and the fixes much easier to review and to backport.

commit.subject: LU-19917 mgc: dynamic MGS NIDs discovery
commit.message:
LU-19917 mgc: dynamic MGS NIDs discovery

Enable fault tolerant MGS on the client: the client MGC can connect to
any server running an MGS follower, and it learns about those servers
on its own.

. a client MGC still tries the first MGS node on the mount line first,
  since with no follower running only the MGS answers, but takes the
  other nodes in a random order, so that clients spread the load
  across the followers there; a server MGC keeps the order given.
  mount.lustre(8) says so now
. the imperative recovery log adds the NIDs of every server that runs
  an MGS, by the LDD_F_SV_TYPE_MGS bit of its entry, to the client MGC
  import at the tail, so this works with no configuration while the
  NIDs from the mount line stay preferred.  A node already known
  keeps the NIDs it has, unlike a target import, since an MGS from the
  mount line may listen on more networks than its targets registered.
  That is independent of mgc.*.dynamic_nids, which covers the target
  imports
. the server MGC device is renamed "mgc<NID>", since it only ever
  connects to the primary MGS, while the client MGC stays "MGC<NID>".
  Userspace and the tests name the one they mean, and it is now what
  "lctl dl" and "lctl get_param mgc.*" show on a server.  A target no
  longer reuses a client's MGC, so it has no OBD_CONNECT_FTM to drop
. a client MGC pings at max(PING_INTERVAL_SHORT, obd_timeout / 20),
  capped at PING_INTERVAL, so it notices a dead MGS in time to not
  miss an IR update.  At the default obd_timeout that is 7s rather
  than 25s, only once followers have run (the IR log has named an MGS
  other than the one it is connected to) and while the client is
  connected to an MGS other than the primary one.  While MGS0 is down
  there are no IR updates to miss, and MGS0 on its primary node does
  not see the faster pings of every client
. a follower builds the fsdb on the first MGS_CONFIG_READ when the
  filesystem is in its CONFIGS directory, and serves the nidtbl it
  has.  A follower whose nidtbl is still empty answers -EAGAIN: its
  entries carry the leader's versions, so an empty table would claim
  a version the client never got entries for.  So does a follower
  that does not have the filesystem, since -ENOENT would make the
  client stop asking for good
. the IR log parser reports why it stops instead of breaking silently.
  Its "datalen < 0" test after the subtraction goes, the bound just
  above it already covers that
. a mount line names at most MGC_MGS_NODES_MAX MGS nodes, where it had
  no bound before; mount.lustre(8) says so and the rest are dropped
  with a console warning
. the tests that read a server MGC match either case, since the server
  they talk to may be an older one; an except file cannot express "the
  server has the rename", because that file is read from the server.
  An old client running its own recovery-small test_141 against a new
  server is the other way round and is excepted: its "*MGC*" globs
  match no server MGC namespace any more
. conf-sanity test_163 is new, and checks that a client MGC moves to
  a follower when the MGS stops; test_160, test_161 and recovery-small
  set_ir_status() are adjusted for a node that can run both an MGS
  follower and a client MGC
. conf-sanity test_73e waits for the targets to re-register after it
  restarts the MGS, and needs LU-19692 on the server to do so: the
  client now mounts as soon as an MGS answers, so it no longer waits
  out the whole reconnect and would otherwise get an empty OSC import
. conf-sanity test_250 updates the MGS version check to match the
  actual version in which the test and functionality landed
